neighbours.label: ' and'/' but' right after a word for amount or number (number, quantity, amount, fewer, more) joining it with a second, qualitative dimension ('the number and variety', 'fewer but larger')
fire: The reserve is famous for the number and diversity of its nesting birds.
Researchers looked at the quantity and quality of sleep in older adults.
Modern farms have fewer, but far larger, fields than they did a century ago.
Each recipe lists the amount and type of flour that works best.
Ageing muscles contain fewer and weaker fibres than young ones.
Investors watched the volume and direction of trading very closely.
There are now more, but smaller, schools in the northern district.
Reviewers judged the number and clarity of the figures in each paper.
quiet: The reserve is famous for the lakes and forests around its nesting sites.
Researchers looked at the diet and habits of older adults who slept well.
Modern farms grow wheat and barley in fields near the river valley.
Each recipe lists the oven and tin that work best for the cake.
Ageing muscles need protein and rest to recover after exercise.
Investors watched the banks and brokers in London very closely.
There are now teachers and nurses living in the northern district.
Reviewers judged the title and abstract of each paper first.
